hypothesis: Adding near-expiry AFTERNOON position sizing (2-3x lots when DTE=1 and session=AFTERNOON) on top of the ATR>30 filter improves risk-adjusted returns, because those trades have dramatically higher EV (avg ₹2,803 from EXP-0002).

FINDING-1.title: ATR>30 filter absorbs the near-expiry PM edge
FINDING-1.detail: EXP-0002 found avg ₹2,803/trade for near-expiry AFTERNOON trades (unfiltered). After applying ATR>30 filter, these same trades average only ₹876/trade. The ATR filter already captures the regime that made those trades valuable; the near-expiry AFTERNOON sub-selection within the filter doesn't add reliable extra edge.
FINDING-1.implication: The near-expiry PM signal and the ATR regime signal are NOT independent. They were measuring the same thing (March high-volatility regime).

FINDING-2.title: Near-expiry boost is inconsistent across months — March-dominated
FINDING-2.detail: 2x boost: helpful in March (+12,048), harmful in Feb (-737), Apr (-539), May (-261). Only 1 of 4 months where qualifying trades existed showed benefit. With n=12 near-expiry PM trades across 6 months, the sample is insufficient for reliable sizing decisions.
FINDING-2.implication: Cannot trust this signal for position sizing with current data volume.

FINDING-3.title: DTE=1 ALL DAY is more interesting than DTE=1 AFTERNOON specifically
FINDING-3.detail: Within ATR>30 universe: DTE=1 all sessions = 48 trades, avg ₹1,076 (40% WR). DTE=1 AFTERNOON only = 12 trades, avg ₹876. Non-AFTERNOON DTE=1 trades avg ~₹1,143. The AFTERNOON restriction (from EXP-0002 unfiltered analysis) does NOT hold within the ATR>30 filtered universe. DTE=1 itself is the better segmentation signal.
FINDING-3.implication: Use DTE as a sizing signal without session restriction. Test DTE=1 (all day) position sizing as EXP-0009.

FINDING-4.title: DTE distribution within ATR>30 filter reveals structural edge
FINDING-4.detail: DTE=0: 37 trades, avg ₹487 (35% WR). DTE=1: 48 trades, avg ₹1,076 (40% WR). DTE=4: 28 trades, avg ₹301 (32% WR). DTE=5: 47 trades, avg ₹161 (26% WR). DTE=6: 46 trades, avg ₹463 (43% WR). DTE=1 is the strongest DTE bucket, followed by DTE=6 (next week's expiry alignment). DTE=5 is the weakest — mid-week, mid-cycle.
FINDING-4.implication: DTE=1 AND DTE=6 may both be worth sizing up. DTE=5 may be worth filtering out.

conclusion: HYPOTHESIS REJECTED. Near-expiry AFTERNOON position sizing (2-3x) on top of ATR>30 does not add reliable value. The ATR filter already captures the regime that made near-expiry PM trades valuable; these two signals are not independent. The 2x boost improves returns by +52pp overall, but that improvement is dominated by 7 March trades and net-hurts performance in 3 of 5 qualifying months. With only 12 qualifying trades, conclusions are unreliable. DO NOT implement variable position sizing based on this finding.
